newsitem.title: USA: Shots across U.S.-Mexico border worry officials.
newsitem.headline: Shots across U.S.-Mexico border worry officials.

text.p: Unknown gunmen in Mexico have been firing dozens of shots into the west Texas border town of El Paso, causing concern on both sides of the border, officials said Wednesday.
Although no one has been injured, law enforcement officials said the situation is dangerous because many people congregate and travel in the area of the shootings.

Doug Mosier, U.S. Border Patrol spokesman, said several dozen shots from a .22 calibre gun were fired Sunday night, then again the following two nights, each time from the Mexican shanty town of Anapra.
The bullets were fired into an area of El Paso known as Roadside Park, located about two miles from downtown.
"It's strange," he said. "We don't know why they're firing. But these shots were definitely fired into the U.S."
Manuel Hernandez, spokesman for the Mexican consulate in El Paso, agreed: "It does have us worried."
Officials said traffic had been rerouted from the busy Paisano Highway because of the shooting.
The Border Patrol has requested that Mexico increase police patrols in Anapra, but Hernandez made no promises.
"There won't be more patrols immediately, but they're looking into it," he said. Mexican officials have said police departments are too short staffed to meet the demands.

Violence in the area of Roadside Park is not new. Two years ago patrols were beefed up in the area after an Anapra gang started sneaking across the border and firing at agents and citizens and attacking them with rocks and bottles. The gang also used boobytraps to stop motorists so they could loot and rob them.
The violence stopped for a while after El Paso police aided the Border Patrol by increasing patrols. Lights were also installed and a chain-link fence was repaired.
